text:
China - Wikipedia
Contents
China
China
,
[
f
]
officially the
People's Republic of China
(
PRC
),
[
g
]
is a country in
East Asia
. It is divided into 33
province-level divisions
, including two
special administrative regions
.
[
h
]
Beijing
is the capital, while
Shanghai
is the
most populous city by urban area
. Its geography features the
Central Plain
, major rivers such as the
Yangtze
and
Yellow River
, deserts,
subtropical
and temperate forests, plateaus, and
mountain ranges
such as the
Himalayas
. It is the
world's second-most populous country
after
India
, with
a population
exceeding 1.4 billion (17% of the world's population). Covering
9.6
million square kilometers (3,700,000
sq
mi)
, it is the
third largest country by area
.
[
i
]
Humans first arrived in China during the
Paleolithic
. During the 2nd millennium
BCE,
dynastic states
emerged. In 221
BCE, China was unified under the
Qin
, followed by the
Han dynasty
, ushering in two millennia of imperial rule across periods of unity and division. The imperial era saw the expansion of the
Silk Road
and the invention of
gunpowder
,
paper
,
printing
, and the
compass
. After increased Western political, economic, and philosophical influence, the empire was succeeded by the
Republic of China
(ROC) after the
1911 Revolution
. The
Warlord Era
and
Chinese Civil War
followed, interrupted by the
Second Sino-Japanese War
, which ended in a Chinese victory. In 1949, the
Chinese Communist Party
(CCP)
proclaimed the PRC
and the
ROC retreated to Taiwan
. Both sides still claim political legitimacy. CCP attempts to advance
its political program
faltered through
famine
and political turmoil. The
reform and opening-up
that began in 1978 moved China towards a
socialist market economy
, spurring economic growth.
China is a
unitary state
with the CCP as its
sole ruling party
. It is one of the five
permanent members
of the
UN Security Council
and a member of
many multilateral organizations
. China is the world's
largest manufacturer
and has the
second-largest economy by nominal GDP
. International organizations have criticized China, alleging authoritarianism and
human rights abuses
. Possessing
a large military
,
space program
, and
nuclear stockpile
, China has been described as a
superpower
due to its influence in geopolitics,
science and technology
,
manufacturing
,
economics
, and
culture
.
Chinese art
and culture have
influenced much of Asia
, with
a literary tradition
dating back millennia to the
Chinese classics
. China is the birthplace of
Confucianism
and
Daoism
, which form the traditional
three teachings
of
Chinese philosophy
and
folk religion
alongside
Buddhism
.
Chinese cuisine
is diverse and highly regional, with rice as a staple in the south and wheat in the north. It has
60 World Heritage Sites
, including the
Great Wall
and
Grand Canal
. The
Han
, speakers of
Sinitic languages
, are China's dominant ethnicity, although it is home to
55 recognized minorities
, including the
Hui
,
Mongols
,
Tibetans
,
Uyghurs
, and
Zhuang
.
Etymology
The word "China" has been used in English since the 16th century; however, it was not used by the Chinese themselves during this period. Its origin has been traced through
Portuguese
,
Malay
, and
Persian
back to the
Sanskrit
word
Cīna
(
चिन
), used in
ancient India
.
[
16
]
Cīna
was first used in early
Hindu
scriptures dating from the 3rd century BCE to 4th century CE, including the
Mahabharata
and the
Laws of Manu
. In 1655, the missionary
Martino Martini
suggested that the word China is derived ultimately from the ancient state of
Qin
.
[
17
]
This remains a common etymology.
[
17
]
[
18
]
Another possible source is the ancient
Guizhou
polity of
Yelang
, known as
ʐina
in
Loloish languages
.
[
17
]
The official name of the modern state is the "People's Republic of China" (
中华人民共和国
;
Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó
).
[
19
]
The shorter form of this name is
中国
;
Zhōngguó
, from
zhōng
('central' or 'middle') and
guó
('state'), a term first used for the
demesne
of the
Western Zhou
dynasty.
[
j
]
[
20
]
[
21
]
The names of ruling imperial dynasties were typically used to refer to the state and its territories. In the 1800s,
Zhongguo
was officially adopted as the name of the country by the
Qing dynasty
.
[
21
]
History
Evidence of early humans such as
Homo erectus
in China dates to the
Paleolithic
, around 1.7
million years ago, with unconfirmed sites as old as 2
million years ago. Modern
Homo sapiens
are attested from around 50,000 years ago.
[
22
]
Following the end of the
Last Glacial Period
, in about 8,000
BCE, pottery-making
Neolithic
cultures emerged. By the 6000s
BCE, sedentary agricultural societies had spread across the lower
Yellow River
basin.
[
23
]
[
24
]
These societies became increasingly complex, urbanized, and stratified,
[
25
]
but many experienced a population collapse in the late 2000s
BCE for unclear reasons.
[
26
]
After 2000
BCE, a
Bronze Age
culture emerged in the
Central Plain
, dubbed the
Erlitou culture
after its
main site
. Erlitou has been controversially identified with the
Xia
, the traditionally-accepted first
dynasty
, but no written records exist to confirm this.
[
27
]
[
28
]
[
29
]
The
Shang dynasty
purportedly succeeded the Xia around 1600
BCE, with its early stages tentatively identified with an expansionist state known archaeologically as the
Erligang culture
.
[
30
]
The historicity of the
Late Shang
is attested through divinational writings in the
oracle bone script
. These are the earliest known form of writing in China and the ancestor of modern
Chinese characters
.
[
31
]
[
32
]
The Shang were overthrown by the
Zhou
c.
1046 BCE
. The Zhou ruled over a vast and loose confederation of vassal states across central China, which was gradually weakened by regional lords.
[
33
]
Centralized authority collapsed in 771
BCE, giving way to constant regional warfare. During the
Eastern Zhou
, the multitude of small polities of the
Spring and Autumn period
evolved into seven territorial
Warring States
.
[
34
]
[
35
]
Literary and philosophical developments of this period include the emergence of various schools of thought, such as
Confucianism
,
Daoism
,
Mohism
, and
Legalism
, alongside
Chinese classics
like the Confucian
Analects
and the Daoist
Dao De Jing
.
[
36
]
[
37
]
In the 220s
BCE,
Qin
rapidly conquered the other warring states. In 221, its ruler
Qin Shi Huang
proclaimed himself the first
emperor
(
皇帝
;
Huángdì
) and founded the
Qin dynasty
.
[
38
]
[
39
]
He led an
autocratic
Legalist state organized in a system of
commanderies
and
counties
. The dynasty lasted only fifteen years, falling soon after his death from
revolts and civil war
.
[
40
]
[
41
]
After the collapse, the
Han dynasty
emerged to rule China between 206
BCE and 220
CE.
[
k
]
[
42
]
The Han gradually reinstated centralized control, legitimizing their rule through Confucian scholarship and political institutions which would be maintained in some form into the 20th century.
[
43
]
[
44
]
Military expeditions against the
Xiongnu
, a confederation of nomadic
steppe
tribes, expanded Han influence into parts of
Central Asia
and helped to establish the
Silk Road
, allowing for trade connections between China and western Eurasia. Contemporaneously, merchants established
maritime trade routes
linking China,
Southeast Asia
, and
India
.
[
45
]
[
46
]
The dynasty is the namesake of the
Han Chinese
, China's main ethnic group.
[
47
]
The Han faced widespread uprisings and the emergence of local warlords in the 100s and 200s CE.
[
48
]
By 220, the empire was split into the
Three Kingdoms
.
[
49
]
These were briefly united by the
Jin dynasty
in 280, which fell into civil war.
Sinicized
formerly-nomadic peoples who had settled in Northern China, such as the Xiongnu, rebelled and
founded new dynasties
.
[
50
]
[
51
]
Various Han Chinese dynasties in Southern China
emerged in the 300s.
[
52
]
During these conflicts,
Buddhism
was introduced to China via the Silk Road.
[
53
]
[
54
]
China was reunited under the
Sui dynasty
in 589,
[
55
]
which constructed the
Grand Canal
to link Northern and Southern China.
[
56
]
The Sui collapsed in the 610s, and was succeeded by the
Tang
. The Tang dynasty centralized the state and dispatched military expeditions to pacify the surrounding regions. It promoted
Buddhism
, but through expanding international trade built a heavily cosmopolitan society centered on its capital of
Chang'an
.
[
57
]
It reformed the
civil service examinations
and oversaw a flourishing of art, poetry, architecture, and scholarship.
[
58
]
[
59
]
[
60
]
The 755–763
An Lushan rebellion
weakened the Tang, which gradually fragmented before collapsing completely in 907, resulting in
another period of war and division
.
[
61
]
[
62
]
The
Song dynasty
rose to power in 960. It faced military crises, unable to subdue its Sinicized non-Han neighbors, the
Khitan
-led
Liao dynasty
and the
Tangut
-led
Western Xia
. The Song's consistent focus on defense resulted in a heavily centralized state and military, which made the first military application of
gunpowder
.
[
63
]
[
64
]
Books became widely available by the proliferation of
printing
technology,
[
65
]
while the elite class of
scholar-officials
grew increasingly powerful.
[
66
]
Production, population, and trade expanded massively, alongside innovations such as industrial
metallurgy
and
hydraulic machinery
.
[
67
]
The Song capital
Kaifeng
was overrun by the
Jurchen
-led
Jin
in 1127, forcing the Song to retreat to Southern China. During this period, the revivalist philosophical movement of
Neo-Confucianism
emerged.
[
68
]
In 1206,
Genghis Khan
united the nomadic
Mongols
to the north under the
Mongol Empire
. Over the following fifty years, they
conquered the Western Xia
and
the Jin
, in addition to
their other conquests
as far west as Europe.
The empire split
into separate khanates, with Mongol leader
Kublai Khan
establishing the
Yuan dynasty
and
subjugating the Song
in the 1270s.
[
69
]
[
70
]
Although Chinese culture remained largely unchanged, the Yuan maintained a Mongol elite culture and established a complex ethnic and occupational hierarchy. Foreign presence increased as China became more connected to Eurasian trade routes.
[
71
]
In the 1340s, central China was devastated by disease, famine, and severe flooding along the Yellow River.
Various rebellions erupted
, leading to a peasant leader establishing the
Ming dynasty
in 1368 and declaring himself the
Hongwu Emperor
.
[
72
]
[
73
]
The Ming later moved their capital from
Nanjing
to
Beijing
, with the
Forbidden City
as the imperial palace. However, the lower Yangtze remained the wealthiest region. Trade grew, and the
European colonization of the Americas
brought new crops and a massive influx of silver to China.
[
74
]
The population doubled, and a growing publishing industry began producing works in
vernacular Chinese
, including the
Four Classic Novels
.
[
75
]
The Ming state declined, and by the 1600s, became unable to contain
peasant rebellions
. The
Manchus
to the north declared the
Qing dynasty
in 1636 and
conquered the Ming
,
[
76
]
killing their last claimant emperor in 1662 and conquering a
Ming rump state on Taiwan
in 1683.
[
77
]
From the late 1600s to the end of the 1700s, the
High Qing era
saw economic growth and territorial expansion westward, including the
conquest of Tibet
and much of
Central Asia
.
[
78
]
[
79
]
[
80
]
European powers fought various wars against the Qing dynasty during the 19th century. These began with the United Kingdom's
First Opium War
in 1839–1842,
[
81
]
[
82
]
which resulted in the first of the "
unequal treaties
" imposed on the dynasty. These opened
treaty ports
, allowed Christian missionary activity, and loosened trade restrictions.
[
83
]
China faced an economic crisis and internal unrest, and uprisings such as the 1850–1864
Taiping Rebellion
resulted in the deaths of millions.
[
84
]
[
85
]
Reformist factions of the Qing responded with the
Self-Strengthening Movement
, seeking to adopt Western weapons and technologies, but this had a limited impact for much of the empire.
[
86
]
The
Empire of Japan
's defeat of the Qing in the
First Sino-Japanese War
(1894–1895) resulted in the loss of
Taiwan
and the growth of both reformist and revolutionary political movements. An
imperial push for reform
in 1898 ended after an internal coup, while the anti-foreign
Boxer Rebellion
was defeated by a
coalition of foreign powers
in 1901. The late Qing dynasty again
advanced reforms
, but growing revolutionary and anti-Manchu sentiment culminated in the
1911 Revolution
. A coalition of revolutionaries led by
Sun Yat-sen
overthrew the Qing and declared the
Republic of China
(ROC) in 1912.
[
87
]
[
88
]
President
Yuan Shikai
rose to power in 1912 and crushed his main opposition, the
Kuomintang
, ruling China as a dictator until his death in 1916, following an abortive attempt to restore the monarchy. During the
Warlord Era
, feuding regional warlords and governors took power across China, while Tibet and
Mongolia
declared independence. The nominal republican government had little control outside Beijing. During this period,
New Culture
intellectuals and students criticized traditional society. A crackdown on a student protest in 1919 led to the
May Fourth Movement
and further agitation by intellectuals for a cultural and political upheaval, with many embracing Western political ideas such as
communism
.
[
89
]
[
90
]
In the mid-1920s, the Kuomintang
allied
with the nascent
Chinese Communist Party
(CCP), and partially reunified China under
Chiang Kai-shek
's leadership. Starting with the
Shanghai massacre
in 1927, the Kuomintang violently purged the CCP and gained the allegiance of the northern warlords, establishing a new government at Nanjing.
[
91
]
The CCP was driven into the countryside and
repressed
, but subsequently
regrouped in the northwest
.
[
92
]
[
93
]
Japan
occupied Manchuria
in 1931, and launched an
invasion of the rest of China
in 1937. A
renewed coalition
between the CCP and Kuomintang fought Japan in what became a theater of
World War II
, as Japanese forces committed numerous
war atrocities
against the civilian population and occupied most of China's major cities.
[
94
]
[
95
]
[
96
]
After the
surrender of Japan
in 1945, China became a founding member of the
United Nations
and regained control over Manchuria and Taiwan. The
civil war
between the CCP and the Kuomintang resumed the following year.
[
97
]
After a string of military victories, CCP chairman
Mao Zedong
formally
proclaimed the People's Republic of China
(PRC) in 1949. The ROC government
retreated to Taiwan
and continued to claim legitimacy.
[
98
]
The following year, the PRC
occupied and annexed Tibet
.
[
99
]
The PRC, which the CCP described as a "
people's democratic dictatorship
", enacted many reforms: it restructured the economy under state control, promoted literacy and gender equality, and expanded heavy industry. The
Land Reform Movement
, in which the state encouraged and organized peasant violence against landlords, leading to the death of upwards of a million people, had begun in northern China during the civil war and extended to most of the rest of China between 1950 and 1952. It distributed landlord land to the peasants as private property, but it was soon followed by collectivization of the land.
[
100
]
[
101
]
[
102
]
In 1958, Mao launched the
Great Leap Forward
, a mass industrialization project which resulted in the
Great Chinese Famine
and millions of deaths. As the
Cold War
deepened, China
grew politically isolated from its former ally
, the
Soviet Union
, as well as the
Western Bloc
. It
detonated its first atomic bomb
in 1964.
[
103
]
[
104
]
Attempting to reassert control over the CCP after the Great Leap, Mao and his allies launched the
Cultural Revolution
in 1966, sparking a decade of political violence, crackdowns on perceived counterrevolutionaries, and social upheaval that lasted until
Mao's death
in 1976.
[
105
]
[
106
]
Deng Xiaoping
served as
paramount leader
from 1978 to 1989. The
reform and opening-up
policies of the 1980s and 1990s saw economic liberalization towards a
socialist market economy
, rapid economic growth, and improved relations with the West.
Political dissent
culminated in a mild crackdown early in 1987 and a much more severe and prolonged crackdown in 1989 that included the
Tiananmen Square massacre
.
[
107
]
China shifted away from an agricultural economy and rapidly urbanized, although this led to stark
economic inequality
between urban and rural areas, as well as environmental deterioration.
[
108
]
Since the 1990s, market forces have become China's main economic driver.
[
109
]
Under the
general secretaryship of Xi Jinping
since 2012, he has launched a far-reaching
anti-corruption campaign
, expanded Chinese economic influence through the
Belt and Road Initiative
, and abolished
term limits
for himself as
state president
.
[
l
]
[
110
]
Geography
China's geography is highly varied, featuring a
dry and mountainous west
, alongside both mountains and wide river valleys in the east. Chinese civilization was traditionally centered in the lowlands around China's two longest rivers: the
Yangtze
and the
Yellow River
, both originating on the
Tibetan Plateau
. This temperate region is bordered by forest and
steppe
to the north, as well as the mountainous and subtropical
south
.
[
111
]
China's shoreline spans the
Bohai Sea
,
Yellow Sea
,
East China Sea
, and
South China Sea
, all part of the
Pacific Ocean
. Its largest island is
Taiwan
, and the largest governed by the PRC is
Hainan
.
[
112
]
Poyang Lake
is the largest of the country's many freshwater lakes.
[
113
]
Large mountain ranges in the west, including the
Himalayas
and
Tian Shan
, separate China from
South
and
Central Asia
. China features both the
Turpan Depression
, among the deepest points on land, and the high Tibetan Plateau.
[
114
]
The world's highest point,
Mount Everest
(
8,848 metres or 29,029 feet
above
sea level
), lies on the border with
Nepal
.
[
115
]
China has a wide variety of ore and mineral resources.
[
116
]
China's climate is dominated by
dry seasons
and wet
monsoons
, which lead to pronounced seasonal temperature differences. In the winter, northern winds coming from high-latitude areas are cold and dry; in summer, southern winds from coastal areas at lower latitudes are warm and moist.
[
117
]
The northwestern deserts receive as little as
50
mm (2.0
in)
of rainfall annually, while much of southern China exceeds
1,000
mm (39
in)
.
[
118
]
Eastern China is well-suited for agriculture, with two or three harvests per year. The south is dominated by
rice
farming, while the north grows crops such as
wheat
and
maize
.
[
119
]
China frequently
faces natural disasters
. Its adjacency to both the
Pacific Ring of Fire
and the
Alpide belt
(tectonic belts) results in frequent earthquakes, the cause of the majority of China's natural disaster deaths. Severe quakes such as the
1976 Tangshan earthquake
cause hundreds of thousands of deaths.
[
120
]
Rainstorms and flooding are common hazards,
[
121
]
with the Yellow River's perennial floods devastating the surrounding plains throughout recorded history.
[
122
]
Typhoons
frequently impact southeastern China.
[
123
]
China is one of 17
megadiverse countries
, containing a wide variety of forests,
shrublands
, wetlands,
steppes
, and deserts, which host (as of 2018) 92,300 known species of plants, animals, and fungi.
[
124
]
According to government surveys,
China's forest coverage
grew from 10% of the overall territory in 1949 to 25% in 2024.
[
125
]
The far north contains
taiga
, which transitions into
deciduous
forest to the south. South of the Yangtze, mixed conifer and deciduous forest is common, with tropical and subtropical forests farther south.
[
126
]
In the 21st century, China has suffered from
environmental deterioration and pollution
due to rapid development, alongside the broader effects of
climate change
. About 11% of its plant species and 21% of its
vertebrate
species are threatened or endangered due to
habitat loss
, pollution, and
poaching
.
[
127
]
"Flagship" endangered species such as the
giant panda
and
tiger
have received additional funding and protection.
[
128
]
Although China has the world's highest
CO
2
emissions
, it only emits 8 tons of
CO
2
per capita
as of 2020, significantly lower than many developed countries.
[
129
]
Total
greenhouse gas emissions by China
are the
world's largest
.
[
129
]
China has prioritized reducing pollution,
[
130
]
announcing its aims to reach its peak emissions levels before 2030, and achieve
carbon neutrality
by 2060.
[
131
]
[
132
]
Water quality in China
has been impacted by rapid development and high levels of
agricultural runoff
and
heavy metal pollution
.
[
133
]
China is the world's leading investor in
renewable energy
and
its commercialization
, investing
CN¥3.6 trillion
(US$546 billion) in 2022 alone.
[
134
]
Traditionally reliant on non-renewable energy sources such as
coal
, China's adoption of
renewable energy
has increased significantly in the 2010s and 2020s.
[
135
]
In 2025, 54.4% of China's electricity came from coal, while 41.6% came from clean energy, with the remainder from other
fossil fuels
.
[
136
]
Despite its emphasis on renewables, China remains dependent on global oil markets.
[
137
]
China is the
second-largest
country by land area after
Russia
, and the third or fourth largest by total area.
[
i
]
Total area figures are generally around
9,596,961
km
2
(3,705,407
sq
mi)
.
[
7
]
[
10
]
China
borders 14 nations
, with a combined land border length of
22,117
km (13,743
mi)
. Its
coastline
spans approximately
14,500
km (9,000
mi)
.
[
10
]
The PRC has engaged in 23 border disputes since 1949, of which six remain unsettled.
[
138
]
It actively
disputes
several portions of its Himalayan border with India, including
Aksai Chin
in
Kashmir
and the Indian state of
Arunachal Pradesh
, which led to
military skirmishes in 2020
.
[
139
]
[
140
]
It maintains maritime disputes with Japan
over the Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands
and with various countries over a group of
South China Sea Islands
within the "
Nine-dash line
", including the
Spratlys
and
Paracels
. This has led to
skirmishes with Vietnam
and the
Philippines
.
[
140
]
[
141
]
Both the PRC and the ROC on Taiwan claim legitimacy as the government of China, leading to
cross-strait tensions
. Taiwan is a
de jure
province
of the PRC,
[
142
]
[
15
]
[
143
]
with the ROC-controlled islands of
Kinmen
and
Matsu
as a part of
Fujian Province
.
[
144
]
[
145
]
Politics
China is a
unitary state
under the
absolute leadership
of the Chinese Communist Party. Since the 1980s, the CCP has called its guiding theories and policies
socialism with Chinese characteristics
, which it considers an adapted form of
Marxism–Leninism
that emphasizes a market economy as the
primary stage of socialism
.
[
146
]
[
147
]
[
148
]
China describes itself as a
socialist state
,
[
148
]
[
149
]
and a
people's democratic dictatorship
.
[
m
]
[
151
]
Many academic sources describe it as an
authoritarian
state,
[
152
]
[
153
]
[
154
]
although others dispute this label as reductive,
[
154
]
or as oversimplifying its methods of political control.
[
153
]
The
National People's Congress
(NPC) holds the
unified powers of the state
and oversight over all state organs, with its
Standing Committee
elected to meet between the annual NPC meetings.
[
155
]
NPC elections are
indirect
and the CCP controls nominations.
[
156
]
[
155
]
The NPC elects the
president
,
vice president
,
military chairman
, and
chief justice
, and approves the president's nomination for
premier
